summary.headline: D.B. Corp Q1 FY27 EBITDA rose about 19% to INR 1,647 million, with margin up 250 bps to 26.1% on advertising growth of about 10%.
summary.overview: Consolidated total revenue grew about 8% YoY to INR 6,220 million and EBITDA about 19% to INR 1,647 million, taking margin to 26.1% from 23.6%. Profit after tax rose about 25% YoY to INR 1,007 million. Advertising revenue grew about 10% to INR 4,320 million, with management attributing the growth to both volume and a small pricing contribution. Circulation was flat at INR 1,204 million, with copies down to about 38 lakh from 39 lakh in Q4 while cover price stayed at an average INR 4.93. Management said newsprint rose about 13% YoY and about 8% QoQ and expects further increases in Q2 before easing from Q3.

financial_highlights.change: flat vs INR 4.9 in Q1 FY26

segments.name: Print and other
segments.commentary: EBITDA of INR 1,499 million, up 18% YoY; this figure covers print and digital, excluding radio, and does not separately show circulation EBITDA. Other operating income rose on higher job work and wastage revenue.

segments.name: Radio
segments.commentary: Revenue rose to INR 425 million from INR 392 million and EBITDA to INR 148 million (+29%). Management cited about 12% advertising growth and 37 operating stations, with 7 more lined up.

segments.name: Digital
segments.commentary: Around 19-20 million monthly active users on news apps as of May 2026, with management describing digital revenue as miniscule and below 5% of total revenue. Hindi and Gujarati micro-drama experiments are under way; an English app is expected later.

guidance_outlook: Capex for FY27 expected at around INR 150-160 crore, similar to the Q4 guidance.
Newsprint prices expected to rise further in Q2 FY27, with easing indicated from Q3 and Q4.
No revenue guidance given; management said only that the team is working hard.
Radio expected to deliver good bottom-line growth in FY27 from a mix of revenue growth and cost control.
Circulation expenses (circulation, promotion) estimated at about INR 20-25 crore annually.
Education advertising shifted from Q1 to Q2 after NEET re-exam, so management expects education growth across Q1 and Q2 combined.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex guided at around INR 150-160 crore.
Strategy to buy and build owned properties where rentals are high; Bhopal property purchased and construction under way, with similar moves in a few other stations.
Print operations span about 250 district editions, generating about 1,700 news pages daily.
Radio network of 37 stations with 7 more lined up.
demand_pricing: Ad growth was broad-based. Education was about 20% of Q1 ad revenue and was flat YoY because NEET results advertising moved to Q2. Government was about 14-15% and growing double digit after DAVP rate increases of about 26% from November 2025 kicked in. Real estate was about 11-12%, jewellery about 5%, and automobile fell to single digit, turning negative YoY.

Circulation fell to about 38 lakh copies from 39 lakh in Q4 and about 43-44 lakh two years ago. Management attributed the decline to summer effects and readers moving to digital, while claiming market share gains in Rajasthan and MP.
Realisation is flat with no price hike taken. Management is avoiding cover price increases to protect readers while advertising is growing.
Newsprint rose about 13% YoY and about 8% QoQ; management put Q1 at around INR 53,000 per tonne versus about INR 49,000 previously.

qa_highlights.question: Has the circulation stream stabilised copies after the dip to about 39 lakh in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 copies were about 38 lakh, with summer impact and some market loss, but management said copies were held and share gained in certain markets.

qa_highlights.question: Did ad growth include one-offs, and how much came from DAVP government ad rates?
qa_highlights.answer: Almost every category grew except education and automobile. Government ads are growing double digit as the DAVP increase kicked in.

qa_highlights.question: What is the newsprint outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Newsprint rose about 13% YoY in Q1 and is expected to rise further in Q2, with easing from Q3 and Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the margin expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited cost savings across the organisation, with staff at all levels involved, and top-line growth. Newsprint is outside its control.

qa_highlights.question: Is ad growth driven by price or volume?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was a little of both, but mostly volume, with pricing contributing a small amount.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other operating income rise sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO attributed it to higher job work revenue and wastage revenue.

risks_watch: Circulation has fallen from about 43-44 lakh two years ago to about 38 lakh, with realisation flat and no price hikes planned.
Newsprint costs are rising, with a further increase expected in Q2 FY27. Margin is exposed until prices ease from Q3.
Automobile advertising turned negative YoY because of fuel supply and geopolitical issues. Education advertising timing depends on NEET results moving into Q2.
Digital is still very small, with about 19-20 million MAUs and no clear monetisation timeline. Management said meaningful revenue contribution is a couple of years away.
Radio growth of about 12% in advertising is a stretch, according to management.
summary.management_tone: Confident on margins, ad growth and cost discipline, but guarded on circulation and digital. Management declined to give revenue guidance and deflected several questions on circulation trends and digital team size.
key_quotes: Consequently, our EBITDA margin expanded by 250 basis points to 26.1% compared to 23.6% in Q1 FY26, demonstrating the strength of our business model.
Now we are very clear we don't want to unnecessarily burden the reader by increasing the price furthermore.
But we clearly see an indication from Q3 and Q4, the prices will start coming down.

adds.what: Radio: 7 more stations lined up (on top of 37 operating)
Owned property purchase in Bhopal and similar moves in a few other stations (buy-and-build, not productive capacity per se)

growth.why: No revenue guidance given; management expects good bottom-line growth in radio in FY27 from revenue growth and cost control, with FY27 capex held at INR 150-160 crore and 7 radio stations lined up, while Q1 consolidated revenue grew about 8% and EBITDA about 19%, driven by ~10% advertising growth that management described as broad-based.
